Those who vowed to walk to the Ka'bah were told to ride: Allah does not need an old man's self-torment, and a woman should walk and also ride.
Aisha vowed never to speak to Abdullah bin Az-Zubair for wanting to stop her charity; the Prophet's Zuhri uncles won her over, and she freed forty slaves in expiation.
Returning from Hunain, Umar asks about his pre-Islamic vow to perform I'tikaf, and the Prophet tells him to fulfil it.
Vowing prevents nothing and brings nothing Allah has not written; it only draws out a miser's wealth.
A vow neither hastens nor delays anything Allah has decreed, only drawing out a miser's wealth; after the best generations will come people who vow without fulfilling and testify unasked.
A vow to obey Allah must be kept, one to disobey Him not; Umar was told to fulfil a pre-Islamic I'tikaf vow; vows of the dead are fulfilled for them.
The Prophet rejected self-torment, cut ropes leading men round the Ka'bah, and let Abu Israil keep only his vow's fast; Ibn Umar cited the ban on fasting Eid.
